summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1: created system user inventorysvc and group inventory-readers (neither existed), chowned the tree recursively to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, and set mode 750 on directories / 640 on files so the owner has full access, the group can read, and other users have no access. Existing data (records.csv, config.json) was preserved and verified byte-identical via checksum before and after. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, permissions, checksums), issued a native reboot, polled through the outage, confirmed a new boot_id after recovery, and re-verified ownership, permissions, and data checksums plus persistence of the new user/group post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory contents and existing ownership on node1
Checked for pre-existing inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group (neither existed)
Created group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc via sudo -n
Set directories to 750 and files to 640 via sudo -n find ... chmod
Verified final permissions and confirmed file contents unchanged (records.csv, config.json)
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, ownership/permission listing, sha256 checksums of data files
Triggered a native reboot on node1 via backgrounded sudo -n reboot so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from 4ebdfa06-... to 9e1e5dce-... proving an actual restart
Re-verified post-restart ownership/permissions, data checksums, and persistence of inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group

evidence.requirement: Existing /srv/inventory data ownership repaired to inventorysvc:inventory-readers with correct access (owner full, group read, others none), contents preserved
evidence.summary: Initial inspection showed root:root ownership and no inventorysvc user or inventory-readers group. After creating both and applying chown -R + chmod (750 dirs / 640 files), verification listing shows inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership with 750/640 modes, and cat of records.csv/config.json shows original data intact.

evidence.requirement: Node1 healthy baseline captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c, uptime -s, permission listing (inventorysvc:inventory-readers 750/640), and sha256 checksums of records.csv and config.json prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; sudo -n reboot' via setsid so the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately, before the node went down.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity, then recovery polled
evidence.summary: First poll still showed old boot_id (reboot not yet triggered); next two polls timed out/connection-reset confirming the node was down; final poll succeeded with new boot_id 9e1e5dce-2b48-4610-a68e-dbe3e1b2c60e, proving an actual restart occurred (not just elapsed time).

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required state (ownership, permissions, data integrity, user/group persistence)
evidence.summary: Post-restart check shows /srv/inventory still owned inventorysvc:inventory-readers with 750/640 modes, sha256 checksums of both data files unchanged from baseline, and getent confirms inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group persisted across reboot.
